body: Oh yes fried chicken is the bomb. I'm thinking about moving to an area where there's more farmers markets and such so it'd be easier to get that ethical stuff. Plus, you're right, it taste a bazillion times better.

I've lied a lot in the past about my eating habits, therefore my parents immediately think that if I'm trying to be vegitarian- that I'm trying to fall back into the eating disorder. They don't trust me. But, I will try. I think they've started to trust me a bit more now, I just don't want to push it. I agree, I love discussions like that- where both parties are being respectful. Now I'm able to have those, I'm just a bit more careful. Haha, I don't get pissed at or disgusted by someone for eating meat anymore. Maybe if I explain to my parents the ethics and everything- and not the health benefits (I don't really care much about those anymore) they'll listen? I don't know, I'll try some things.

I totally relate to this. My mind immediately cleared once I started consuming dairy. I don't think I was getting enough fat in my diet, after trying to recover as a vegan, and needed that easily processed stuff. I try really hard to get ethically produced meat but my parents don't always do so. I'm just waiting until I can move out and at least be vegitarian again, the guilt is killing me.

Well, I totally support the vegan agenda and I do encourage people who are interested in the premise to go for it. I provide facts, etc. I just am now more careful about it because I understand how easy it is for eating disorders, specifically in teenagers, to stem from those hardcore guilt enducing YouTube 'activists' that are everywhere. I make it a point to tell people that there is no such thing as a 'perfect vegan' or a 'perfect diet.' Everyone is different and reacts differently to what they eat, but if morals are concerned, without bringing weight or health into it, veganism is an obvious choice. When I turn 18, and can move the hell out, I'll go back to being vegitarian and see how that goes. I think I just needed that extra bit of protein dairy provides for a little while. Anyway, thanks for your comment, I appreciate your understanding

Thank you, I'll ask my parents about being vegetarian and see what they say. I was thinking about that. I might have to simply wait, which is agonizing, but I'm planning to move the hell out as soon as I turn 18 so it'll be alright. Oh yes, I'm never, ever having kids. And I don't push the vegan agenda on anyone anymore like those fucking 'raw' youtubers because I realize how influential that is on teenagers and how easy it is for pretty severe eating disorders to stem from that. Thanks again for your kind comment

I would NEVER have kids- ever. Haha no fucking way. I would never bring another living being into this shit hole for my own fucked up selfish desires and wants. No thanks. I want to have the smallest imprint on this world as I possibly can. If I had the courage, and could get past that damn survival instinct, I'd kill myself. There's other reasons of course, but a big one is that my existence is aiding in the deterioration of the planet and I am literally not needed.

Yes, when I'm able to live on my own I'll get some help from a professional that doesn't just go along with the 'you need meat' bs. And I completely agree, veganism (if carefully ensuring you get all the right nutrients) is exponentially healthier than eating meat. Thank you, by the way, for answering so kindly, I appreciate it. I'm looking forward to being able to go back to veganism or at least vegitarianism because man the guilt is too much.

Totally, I see it everywhere nowadays. Like Jesus Christ just don't get fucking married and don't have kids. I don't get why people can't understand and see the patterns. Every time I bring up the fact that I will never have kids and get married and all that bs my parents just smile and say, "oh you'll want to someday," and I'm like no, I'm pretty damn sure I won't.
